 Cubs could pivot to imminent Rays target as Carson Kelly's price climbs 
 A cheap Carson Kelly replacement for the Cubs to consider. By Jordan Campbell | Nov 18, 2026, 3:01 PM EST Share on Facebook Share on X Share on Reddit Copy Article Add us as a preferred source World Series: Milwaukee Brewers v Tampa Bay Rays - Game Three | Elsa/GettyImages There's expected to be an uptick in trade activity leading up to the non-tender deadline on Friday, and the Tampa Bay Rays could have a catcher on the Chicago Cubs' radar. Reports out of Tampa indicated that not only are the Rays shopping backup catcher Nick Fortes , there's a reasonable expectation that he could be dealt before the end of the week. 
--> There's expected to be an uptick in trade activity leading up to the non-tender deadline on Friday, and the Tampa Bay Rays could have a catcher on the Chicago Cubs' radar. Reports out of Tampa indicated that not only are the Rays shopping backup catcher Nick Fortes , there's a reasonable expectation that he could be dealt before the end of the week. 
 Editor's note: The Rays have found a trade partner for Nick Fortes, sending him to the Boston Red Sox. It's worth noting the Red Sox are now expected to part ways with Connor Wong, who could be a fit for the Cubs and what they are looking for behind the plate. 
--> Editor's note: The Rays have found a trade partner for Nick Fortes, sending him to the Boston Red Sox. It's worth noting the Red Sox are now expected to part ways with Connor Wong, who could be a fit for the Cubs and what they are looking for behind the plate. 
 Fortes is entering his third year of arbitration, carrying a salary projection of $3.4 million, and moving him now is the type of move the Rays have mastered over the years. With specific regard to Fortes, there are several teams in need of catching this offseason, and after Ryan Jeffers surprisingly returned to the Minnesota Twins , Tampa Bay is an ideal position to shop a catcher who would be under team control for two more seasons. 
--> Fortes is entering his third year of arbitration, carrying a salary projection of $3.4 million, and moving him now is the type of move the Rays have mastered over the years. With specific regard to Fortes, there are several teams in need of catching this offseason, and after Ryan Jeffers surprisingly returned to the Minnesota Twins , Tampa Bay is an ideal position to shop a catcher who would be under team control for two more seasons. 
 The Cubs are among those teams . With Jeffers off the market, it seems less likely that Carson Kelly returns to Chicago. While the Cubs certainly would love to have Kelly back, his asking price likely won't be aligned with a team that has several needs in the starting rotation, and also expected to lose two of their starting outfielders from the 2026 season.

While the Cubs certainly would love to have Kelly back, his asking price likely won't be aligned with a team that has several needs in the starting rotation, and also expected to lose two of their starting outfielders from the 2026 season. 
 Nick Fortes would be a cheap trade alternative if the Cubs don't want to pay Carson Kelly
--> Nick Fortes would be a cheap trade alternative if the Cubs don't want to pay Carson Kelly
 Even if the Cubs aren't opposed to the idea of entering the 2027 season with Miguel Amaya and Owen Ayers as their catching tandem, across the entire organization, the team also needs depth at the position. It's why it's no surprise to see North Side Baseball's Matthew Trueblood suggest that the Cubs are among the teams talking to the Rays about a Fortes trade . 
--> Even if the Cubs aren't opposed to the idea of entering the 2027 season with Miguel Amaya and Owen Ayers as their catching tandem, across the entire organization, the team also needs depth at the position. It's why it's no surprise to see North Side Baseball's Matthew Trueblood suggest that the Cubs are among the teams talking to the Rays about a Fortes trade . 
 Fortes' reputation throughout his career has been as a glove-first catcher, something the Cubs prefer at the position, but his offensive numbers showed a slight uptick in 2026. He slashed .258/.304/.376 with a wRC+ of 90. Certainly not the fixture that Kelly was in the Cubs' lineup over the last two years, but numbers you can live with. Especially when Fortes' Baseball Savant is often dripping read with his defensive metrics.

 It's also worth noting that Fortes still has two minor-league options. In other words, even if Cubs wanted to move forward with Amaya and Ayers, Fortes could open next year in the minors. Though, a likelier scenario may see the Cubs view Amaya as a potential trade candidate, considering Fortes has seen regular time in the majors since the start of the 2022 season.
